name: Margherita Pizza
blurb: A blistered, chewy base with a bright uncooked tomato sauce, torn mozzarella and basil.
ingredients: For the dough (makes 2): 300g strong white bread flour, 1/2 tsp instant yeast, 1 tsp salt, 200ml warm water, 1 tbsp olive oil
1 x 400g tin good plum tomatoes, hand-crushed and drained a little
1 garlic clove, grated; pinch of salt and sugar; drizzle of olive oil
2 balls mozzarella (about 250g), torn and patted dry
Fine semolina or flour, for dusting
method: Mix the dough ingredients into a rough ball, knead 8 minutes until smooth and elastic, then leave covered for 1-2 hours until doubled (or overnight in the fridge). Divide in two and shape into tight balls; rest 30 minutes.
Put a heavy oven tray or pizza steel on the top shelf and heat the oven as high as it goes (250C+) for 30 minutes.
Season the crushed tomatoes with the garlic, salt, sugar and oil.
Stretch one dough ball on a semolina-dusted board to a thin 28cm round, leaving a puffier rim. Spread with a thin layer of sauce and scatter over half the mozzarella.
Slide onto the hot tray and bake 6-9 minutes until the crust is charred in spots and the cheese is molten. Finish with basil and a little olive oil. Repeat for the second.

name: Pepperoni Pizza
blurb: The classic: crisp-rimmed base, tomato, mozzarella and cupped, spicy pepperoni crisping at the edges.
ingredients: 1 batch pizza dough (as Margherita), divided into 2 balls
1 x 400g tin plum tomatoes, crushed and seasoned with garlic, salt, sugar and oil
2 balls mozzarella (250g), torn and patted dry
100g pepperoni or spicy salami, thinly sliced
Chilli flakes and a little honey, to finish (optional)
method: Make and prove the dough as for the Margherita. Heat the oven with a heavy tray inside at maximum for 30 minutes.
Stretch a dough ball thin on a floured board, leaving a raised rim.
Spread with a thin layer of tomato, scatter over half the mozzarella, then lay on half the pepperoni and a pinch of oregano.
Bake on the hot tray for 6-9 minutes until the crust is blistered and the pepperoni has curled and crisped.
Finish with chilli flakes and a thread of honey if you like. Repeat for the second pizza.

name: Garden Vegetable Pizza
blurb: Tomato base loaded with courgette, pepper and red onion, finished with rocket and lemon.
ingredients: 1 batch pizza dough (as Margherita), divided into 2 balls
1 x 400g tin plum tomatoes, crushed and seasoned
Handful of rocket, lemon and olive oil, to finish
method: Make and prove the dough; heat the oven with a heavy tray at maximum for 30 minutes.
Toss the courgette, pepper and onion with a little oil and salt.
Stretch a dough ball thin, spread with tomato and scatter over half the mozzarella and half the vegetables.
Bake on the hot tray for 7-9 minutes until the crust is charred and the vegetables are tender and lightly browned.
Top with rocket dressed in lemon and oil. Repeat for the second.

name: Nduja & Hot Honey Pizza
blurb: Fiery nduja melting into the cheese, cut through with a sharp drizzle of chilli honey.
ingredients: 1 batch pizza dough (as Margherita), divided into 2 balls
1 x 400g tin plum tomatoes, crushed and seasoned
3 tbsp runny honey warmed with 1/2 tsp chilli flakes
Fresh basil or oregano, to finish
method: Make and prove the dough; heat the oven with a heavy tray at maximum for 30 minutes.
Stretch a dough ball thin, spread with a thin layer of tomato and scatter over half the mozzarella.
Dot half the nduja over the top so it can melt and spread as it bakes.
Bake on the hot tray for 6-9 minutes until blistered and bubbling.
Drizzle with the warm chilli honey, add herbs, and repeat for the second.

name: Beer-Battered Fish & Chips
blurb: Crisp, lacy beer batter around flaky white fish, with proper chunky chips and mushy peas.
ingredients: 4 skinless cod, haddock or pollock fillets (about 150g each)
1.2kg floury potatoes (Maris Piper), cut into 1.5cm chips
200g plain flour, plus extra for dusting
330ml very cold beer or sparkling water
300g frozen peas, 20g butter, sprig of mint (for mushy peas)
Lemon wedges and malt vinegar, to serve
method: Rinse the chips, dry very well, and fry at 140C for 6-7 minutes until soft but not coloured. Lift out and cool.
Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt, then whisk in the cold beer to a batter just thicker than double cream. Keep it cold.
Heat the oil to 180C. Dust the fish in flour, dip in batter, let the excess drip, and fry two pieces at a time for 5-6 minutes until deep gold and crisp. Drain on a rack in a low oven.
Turn the oil up to 190C and fry the chips again for 3-4 minutes until crisp and golden. Drain and salt.
Simmer the peas with a splash of water, drain, crush with the butter and mint. Serve everything hot with lemon and vinegar.

name: Jamaican Oxtail Stew
blurb: Oxtail browned and slow-braised with allspice, thyme, scotch bonnet and butter beans until falling off the bone.
ingredients: 2 tbsp browning or 1 tbsp dark soy + 1 tsp treacle
4 spring onions, 6 garlic cloves, 1 thumb ginger
2 tbsp tomato purée, 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce
method: Toss the oxtail with the browning and plenty of salt and pepper. Brown very well in batches in a heavy pot — take your time, this is the flavour.
Soften the onions, carrot, spring onions, garlic and ginger in the fat for 8 minutes. Stir in the allspice, thyme and tomato purée for 1 minute.

Return the oxtail, add the Worcestershire, whole scotch bonnet and stock to just cover. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook at 150C (or lowest hob) for 3 hours, turning once, until the meat is yielding.
Lift out the scotch bonnet. Add the butter beans and simmer uncovered for 20-30 minutes until the sauce is thick and glossy and the oxtail is falling apart.
Skim the fat, rest 15 minutes, and serve with rice and peas.

name: Brown Stew Chicken
blurb: Jamaican chicken marinated in green seasoning, seared dark and simmered in a rich onion-pepper gravy.
ingredients: 4 spring onions, 4 garlic cloves, 1 thumb ginger, small bunch thyme — blitzed to a paste with 1 tbsp oil
1 tbsp browning or 1 tbsp dark soy
Rice and peas or plain rice, to serve
method: Rub the chicken with the green seasoning paste and browning and marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Scrape off most of the marinade (reserve it) and sear the chicken hard in a little oil until very dark on all sides. Lift out.
Fry the onions and peppers in the pan for 8 minutes, add the reserved marinade, ketchup and allspice for 2 minutes.
Return the chicken with the whole scotch bonnet, carrot and stock. Cover and simmer for 25 minutes, then uncover for 10 more to thicken the gravy.
Remove the scotch bonnet before it bursts, check the seasoning, and serve over rice.

name: Escovitch Fish
blurb: Crisp-fried snapper or sea bream doused in a hot, sweet-sour vinegar dressing of peppers and onion.
ingredients: 4 whole small snapper or sea bream, scaled and slashed (or 4 firm white fillets)
1 tsp allspice, 1 tsp salt (to season the fish)
1 tbsp sugar, 1 tsp allspice berries, a few pepper leaves or bay
Rice and peas or festival, to serve
method: Pat the fish very dry and season with allspice and salt. Shallow fry in hot oil for 4-5 minutes each side until crisp and golden. Drain and lay in a deep dish.
In a clean pan, warm 3 tbsp oil and soften the onions, peppers, carrot and scotch bonnet for 4-5 minutes so they still have crunch.
Add the vinegar, sugar, allspice berries and bay and bring to a quick boil.
Pour the hot pickle and all its liquid over the fish.
Leave at least 30 minutes (or overnight in the fridge) for the flavours to soak in, then serve at room temperature with rice.

name: Trinidad Chicken Pelau
blurb: One-pot rice cooked in burnt-sugar caramel with chicken, pigeon peas and coconut.
ingredients: 3 tbsp green seasoning (blitzed spring onion, garlic, thyme, coriander, culantro)
1 x 400g tin pigeon peas (or kidney beans), drained
1 scotch bonnet whole, 2 tbsp ketchup, thyme
method: Marinate the chicken in the green seasoning for 20 minutes.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot, add the sugar and let it caramelise to a dark bubbling amber.
Add the chicken and stir hard so it coats in the caramel and browns, 4-5 minutes.
Stir in the rice, peas, carrot, pepper, ketchup and thyme, then pour in the coconut milk and stock. Add the whole scotch bonnet and season.
Bring to a boil, cover and cook on low for 20-25 minutes until the rice is tender and a little sticky. Rest 10 minutes, remove the scotch bonnet, and fluff.

name: Chicken Yassa
blurb: Senegalese chicken braised in a mountain of slow-cooked onions sharp with lemon, mustard and chilli.
ingredients: 1 Scotch bonnet or 2 tbsp mustard, whole
method: Mix the lemon juice, mustard, garlic and half the sliced onions with salt and pepper. Add the chicken and marinate for at least 1 hour (ideally overnight).
Lift the chicken out and sear it in the oil until deeply browned; set aside.
Add all the onions (marinade included) to the pan and cook down over medium heat for 20-25 minutes until soft, jammy and lightly caramelised.
Return the chicken with the bay, whole Scotch bonnet and 200ml water. Cover and simmer 25 minutes until tender, then uncover to reduce to a thick onion sauce.
Fish out the Scotch bonnet, stir in the olives, and serve over rice.

name: Doro Wat
blurb: Ethiopia's national dish: chicken slow-simmered in a deep, fiery berbere and caramelised-onion sauce with whole eggs.
ingredients: 60g niter kibbeh (spiced clarified butter) or 60g butter/oil
4 garlic cloves and 1 thumb ginger, grated
4 hard-boiled eggs, peeled and lightly scored
method: Toss the chicken with the lemon juice and a little salt; set aside.
Cook the onions in a dry heavy pan over low heat, stirring often, for 20 minutes until collapsed and golden — no oil yet.
Add the niter kibbeh, garlic and ginger and cook 5 minutes, then stir in the berbere and tomato purée and fry gently for 3-4 minutes until darkened and glossy.
Add the chicken, turn to coat, then pour in the stock. Cover and simmer very gently for 35-40 minutes until the sauce is thick and clinging.
Nestle in the boiled eggs for the last 10 minutes to take on colour. Serve with injera to scoop.

name: Bobotie
blurb: South African spiced beef mince baked under a savoury egg custard, with bay leaves and chutney.
ingredients: 2 tbsp mild curry powder, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp ground cumin
2 slices white bread soaked in 200ml milk
3 tbsp fruit chutney, 2 tbsp sultanas, 30g flaked almonds
Yellow rice (rice cooked with turmeric and a cinnamon stick), to serve
method: Fry the onions until soft, add the mince and brown well, then stir in the curry powder, turmeric and cumin for 2 minutes.
Squeeze the milk from the bread (keep the milk) and mash the bread into the meat with the chutney, sultanas, almonds and lemon juice. Season well.
Beat 1 egg and mix it through, then pack the mixture into a baking dish and smooth the top.
Beat the remaining 2 eggs with the reserved milk and pour over. Tuck in the bay leaves.
Bake at 180C for 30-35 minutes until the custard is just set and golden. Rest 10 minutes and serve with yellow rice.

name: Chicken & Dumplings
blurb: Southern-style: shredded chicken in a creamy broth with pillowy dropped dumplings and peas.
ingredients: For the dumplings: 200g self-raising flour, 1 tsp baking powder, 60g cold butter, small bunch parsley, about 120ml milk
method: Poach the chicken in the stock with a bay leaf for 20 minutes, then lift out, shred and set aside. Keep the stock.
Melt the butter, soften the onion, carrot and celery for 8 minutes, then stir in the flour and cook 2 minutes.
Whisk in the reserved stock and simmer to a light gravy. Add the cream, nutmeg and shredded chicken.
Rub the butter into the dumpling flour and baking powder, stir in the parsley and enough milk for a soft dough. Drop tablespoons on top of the gently bubbling stew.
Cover and simmer for 15 minutes without peeking until the dumplings are risen and cooked through. Stir in the peas and serve.

name: Red Beans & Rice
blurb: New Orleans Monday supper: red beans slow-simmered creamy with the trinity and smoked sausage.
ingredients: 500g dried red kidney beans, soaked overnight (or 3 tins, drained — reduce simmer to 30 min)
1 onion, 1 green pepper, 2 celery sticks, diced
2 bay leaves, 1 tbsp Cajun seasoning, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp dried thyme
1 smoked ham hock or 100g smoked bacon (optional)
Steamed long-grain rice and sliced spring onion, to serve
method: Brown the sausage in a heavy pot and set aside. Soften the onion, pepper and celery in the fat for 8 minutes, then add the garlic and spices for 1 minute.
Add the drained beans, bay, ham hock if using, and stock to cover by 4cm.
Simmer gently, part-covered, for about 1 hour 15 until the beans are very soft, stirring now and then.
Mash a ladle of beans against the side and stir back in to thicken the pot to a creamy gravy. Return the sausage, shred any ham hock meat back in, and add the vinegar.
Season and serve spooned over rice with spring onions.

name: Shrimp Étouffée
blurb: Prawns smothered in a blond-roux Cajun sauce with the holy trinity, over fluffy rice.
ingredients: 1 onion, 1 green pepper, 2 celery sticks, finely diced
500ml shellfish or chicken stock (simmer the shells in it for 15 min, then strain)
1 tbsp Cajun seasoning, 1/2 tsp cayenne, 1 tsp smoked paprika
2 spring onions and small bunch parsley, chopped
method: Melt the butter, whisk in the flour and cook, stirring constantly, for 6-8 minutes to a peanut-coloured roux.
Add the onion, pepper and celery and cook for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and spices for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the stock and simmer for 12-15 minutes to a smooth, gravy-thick sauce.
Stir in the prawns and cook 3-4 minutes just until pink and firm.
Fold through the spring onions and parsley, check the seasoning, and serve over rice.

name: Yankee Pot Roast
blurb: A whole braising joint slow-cooked with root vegetables until sliceable-soft, in its own rich gravy.
ingredients: 1.5kg beef brisket or chuck, in one piece
4 carrots and 3 celery sticks, in chunks
3 bay leaves, sprig of rosemary and thyme
method: Season the beef all over and brown it hard on every side in a heavy casserole. Lift out.
Brown the onions, carrots and celery in the fat for 8 minutes, stir in the tomato purée for 1 minute, then pour in the wine and let it bubble.
Return the beef, add the stock and herbs to come halfway up, cover and cook at 150C for 2 hours 30, turning once.
Add the potatoes and cook, still covered, for a further 45 minutes until everything is very tender.
Rest the beef 15 minutes, skim the fat, thicken the gravy with a little slaked cornflour if you like, then slice the beef against the grain and serve with the vegetables and gravy.
